title: Security gate review - weekly standup notes (2026-06-16)
agenda: Quick sync on intake changes, secrets rollout pilot, threat-model backlog, and sprint gating updates. Reserve 10m for open questions and action assignment.
notes:
1) Intake scoring tweak: proposal to move external-reported vuln scoring from numerical 1-5 to a three-tier (urgent/high/medium) plus CVSS mapping. Reason: reduces triage time and standardizes SLAs across Dedicated/Private customers.

2) Automation: Arjun demoed a Slack workflow that auto-assigns newly created SEC JIRAs to oncall via /sec-report; PoC in #sec-triage-thread showed 86% faster ack. Next: connect to infra bot to append 'affected-service' tag from stacktrace.

3) Secrets scanning pilot (CredShield): rollout to CI for red-team repo started 2026-06-10. Findings: 12 historical secrets flagged (mostly long-lived service tokens), 3 false positives (test fixtures). Plan: run two-week pilot on 3 more repos then enable org-wide read-only scanner. Lena to validate that scanner doesn't leak scanned values to logs.

4) Secrets rotation policy: agreed baseline: short-lived tokens where possible (TTL <= 7d) and enforced rotation for service tokens older than 90d. Priya will draft policy language for product teams and required exceptions process.

5) Threat modeling: Samir presented initial dataflow for External Connectors (third-party integrations). Primary concerns: outbound data exfil via callback endpoints, auth token scope creep, and misconfigured webhooks. Action: request component-level DFDs from Integrations team by 2026-06-22.

6) Patch & rollout cadence: SRE reports kernel + driver patches for GPU fleet will be staged next week (canary on 2 Dedicated nodes). Impact window: 30–45m per pool. No customer-facing degradation expected but will enable fallback routing.

7) Backlog prioritization: SEC board shows 18 open intake items, 6 marked urgent/high. We agreed to surface top-6 to Exec Review next Thurs for capacity allocation.

8) Observability: request to Console team to expose per-model token-source breakdown to help attribute suspicious spikes — assigned to Arjun (INF-4521 link).

9) Risk table note (quick): high-risk items currently: exposed long-lived tokens (medium-to-high probability, high impact), incomplete threat models for external connectors (medium probability, high impact), and incomplete secrets rotation for vendor integrations (low probability, high impact).

10) Notes-to-self / roughs: include a short checklist for intake forms: contact, exploitability, PoC, environment, CI evidence, affected versions, mitigation url. Put into sec-gate-playbook-v2.

11) Open questions: - Should CredShield be allowed to write findings into GH issues automatically? (privacy concern). - How do we contractually require partners to rotate tokens for connectors? Legal input needed.

12) Misc: Tobias flagged an upcoming audit window (2026-07-12 to 2026-07-16). We should finalize rotation policy before audit run; mark as high priority.
decisions: Adopt three-tier intake scoring (urgent/high/medium) mapping to CVSS for tracking
Pilot CredShield in CI for 3 more repos, then org-wide read-only scan if no issues
Enforce rotation policy draft: TTL <= 7d preferred; mandatory rotation for service tokens older than 90d (exceptions path required)
Request DFDs from Integrations team by 2026-06-22 for External Connectors threat modeling
